title: Teenagers and Money
description: Reading an interview and saying what you think of the person in it: the five questions of the pocket-money questionnaire (how often, would you like more, what you spend it on, sharing with brothers and sisters, a right or a favour) and the two judgements it calls for, selfish or not and right or favour; the ten answers of the seventeen-year-old singer Carol Chapel, from the £80 a month she still gets to the £20 million the press credits her with and the fortune she can only touch at twenty-one; matching an answer to its question when eleven questions face ten answers and one is always left over, by naming the topic and checking the shape of the answer; the words of the lesson (naïve, ruthless, close, looks, to matter, self-confident, obsessed with, an extravagance, publicity) with the three false friends a French speaker walks into; asking for an opinion with How do you like...? and giving one with I think, I feel, I believe that...; and writing the group report of opinions with their reasons, then the new IT'S YOUR TURN TO ASK THE QUESTIONS box
